purpose: Design pass for torchvision+torchaudio coverage (action item 18). NOT a build manifest yet -- mirror-vs-repack classification per cell is deferred to implementation (see stats.mirror_vs_repack_split).
compat_table_note: comfy-env's own table stops at torch 2.12; this grid's 2.13.0/2.14.0 rows extrapolate (+1 torchvision minor, torchaudio held at 2.11 per the 2.12 precedent where torchaudio never shipped a matching release) -- flag for comfy-env maintainers to confirm/update.

stats.abi_coupling: EXACT torch version pin (Requires-Dist: torch==X.Y.Z), verified from real wheel METADATA -- torchvision/torchaudio must be paired with the identical torch patch+build our libtorch/pytorch already published for that cell, not just the same minor
stats.mirror_vs_repack_split: NOT YET CLASSIFIED per-cell (deferred): conda-forge carries torchvision 0.19-0.28 (linux full range, win-64 from 0.20.1) and torchaudio 2.4.1-2.11.0 (linux full range, win-64 ONLY 2.11.0) -- same minor+flavour-exact discipline as the main grid applies; doing the same two-pass build-string check main grid.json used is the next concrete step

torchvision_0.23.0+cu128_cp312.rpath_on__C.so: /__w/_temp/conda_environment_16469656626/lib (DEAD build-machine absolute path -- must be scrubbed like the main torch repacks; resolution works ONLY because torch's own libc10/libtorch/libtorch_cpu/libtorch_cuda are already resident by soname when torchvision._C is dlopen'd -- same mechanism verified for functorch/_C in the main project
needed_beyond_torch: libcudart.so.12 (already a libtorch dependency -- no NEW conda dep required)

torchaudio_2.8.0+cu128_cp312.sox: vendored in-wheel (libtorchaudio_sox.so) -- no external system sox needed
torchaudio_2.8.0+cu128_cp312.ffmpeg_backends: THREE version-specific backends bundled (_torio_ffmpeg{4,5,6}.so), each hard-linking an exact ffmpeg major's sonames (libavutil.so.58/57/56 etc) which are NOT vendored -- torchaudio probes at runtime for whichever is loadable and degrades gracefully if none. This is the one real external-dependency question for the audio side: repack should either leave ffmpeg undeclared (matches upstream's own optional-probe design) or add conda-forge ffmpeg as a soft/run_constrained dep -- recommend the former (undeclared) to avoid forcing a multi-hundred-MB ffmpeg install on users who don't need audio I/O
torchaudio_2.8.0+cu128_cp312.rpath: none on any inspected .so -- same already-loaded-by-soname resolution as torchvision

pipeline_design_recommendation: New script tools/repack_family.py (NOT an extension of torch_repack.py -- the two packages don't need a libtorch-style split, no CUDA payload of their own, no per-python shared-artifact donor logic). Shape: download the exact-pinned torchvision/torchaudio wheel for (torch_version, flavour, platform, python), scrub the dead absolute RPATH to a clean $ORIGIN-relative list (same lint as verify_repack.py already enforces), apply the same dist-info/license/purls/provenance/`.pyc` gates items 1-14 established, and depend on the EXACT already-published pytorch build_string for that cell (hard failure if that pytorch hasn't published yet -- torchvision/torchaudio repacks must be dispatched strictly after their paired pytorch cell, not in parallel).
rollout_order: 1. torchvision first: zero external-dependency complexity (only needs cudart, already a libtorch dep), 436 buildable records, high conda-forge mirror overlap on linux -- lowest risk, highest immediate payoff since more comfy packs use vision ops than audio ops (assumption: not verified against comfy-forge pack manifests in this pass -- recommend a quick grep of comfy-forge-registry/comfy-forge-docs pack listings for torchvision-vs-torchaudio import frequency before committing the resourcing order).

2. torchaudio second: same mechanics plus the ffmpeg-backend decision above; win-64 is almost entirely a repack job (conda-forge only carries 2.11.0 there) so it lands more repack-CI weight than torchvision's win-64 line.
